rationale: The fix correctly aligns the step condition with the actual target selector, eliminating the permanent-block scenario. The defensive fallback timer in OnboardingTooltip is a well-scoped safety net. No new patterns introduced; changes are minimal and focused.

business_review.criterion: Onboarding tour no longer gets stuck on the analytics step when NavigationAssistants returns null.
business_review.evidence: Condition changed from div[class*='flex'] (always true) to !!document.querySelector('[data-onboarding="prebuilt-assistants"]') (matches only when the actual target exists). When NavigationAssistants renders null, the step is excluded from activeSteps entirely.

business_review.criterion: User cannot be permanently blocked by a missing target element.
business_review.evidence: OnboardingTooltip now sets fallbackReady=true after 400ms when the target element is absent. tooltipReady becomes true via the fallbackReady condition, making the tooltip visible and interactive regardless of target presence.

business_review.criterion: The overlay does not block clicks when the tooltip is not visible.
business_review.evidence: With the condition fix the affected step is skipped entirely, so the overlay is never rendered for it. The fallback timer ensures the tooltip is always made visible if a step is rendered without its target.

standards_review.notes: Commit subject follows JIRA-key: fix(scope): description format. Pre-commit hooks passed (prettier, eslint, tsc, license-headers, secrets).
Changes are minimal — 2 files, 16 net insertions. No new abstractions. fallbackReady state follows existing useState patterns in the component.
No security issues. No auth, secrets, injection, or unsafe handling in the diff.
